provenance.original: Applicants who enroll or renew in a TSA Agent State consist of three types of respondents: new enrollments, online renewals, and in-person renewals.  TSA estimates 48 percent of applicants will be new enrollments, and 52 percent will be renewals.  All new enrollments must be done in person, with the option of conducting an online pre-enrollment, while renewals may be done online.  TSA estimates 60 percent of the renewals will be done online, while the remaining 40 percent will be done in person.  Table 4 shows the calculations.
provenance.transformation: Source retained verbatim; comparison inference separately labeled

provenance.original: TSA calculates the number of individuals who would choose to enroll on-line under TSA Agent States by multiplying the number of TSA Agent State enrollments in Table 1 by 44 percent (from Table 3).  This calculation is shown in columns (A) and (B) of Table 5(a).
provenance.transformation: Source retained verbatim; comparison inference separately labeled

provenance.original: TSA calculates the number of individuals who would choose to enroll in-person under TSA Agent States by multiplying the number of TSA Agent State enrollments in Table 1 by 56 percent (see Table 3).  This calculation is shown in column (G) of Table 5(b).
provenance.transformation: Source retained verbatim; comparison inference separately labeled

provenance.original: TSA will be implementing the ability for online renewals or re-enrollment capability for applicants.  Active HME holders will be able to renew online before their STA expires; HME holders who have a recently expired STA will be able to re-enroll online.  Approximately 52 percent of active HME holders renew their HME when it expires every 5 years.  Online HME renewals will reduce the applicant’s cost and hour burden by avoiding visiting a TSA enrollment center for the renewal of an STA.  TSA estimates the online renewal time burden to be 10 minutes (0.17 hours), and calculates the total time burden by multiplying the number of online renewals as shown in column (N) of Table 5(c).  Also, due to the reduced cost of the online enrollment transaction, the renewal fee for an HME STA will decrease.  TSA estimates 60 percent of renewals through TSA Agent States will be done online.  The calculations are summarized in Table 5(c).
provenance.transformation: Source retained verbatim; comparison inference separately labeled

provenance.original: Designate a Cybersecurity Coordinator/Alternate Cybersecurity Coordinator: All Owner/Operators subject to this requirement have designated a Cybersecurity Coordinator and at least one alternate coordinator.  However, due to employee turnover, TSA anticipates that some entities will need to periodically designate new Cybersecurity Coordinators or alternates.  In these instances, TSA SMEs estimate respondents will spend 5 minutes (0.083 hours) performing this task.  TSA assumes that the designation of a new Cybersecurity Coordinator (or alternate) represents a small burden that only includes emailing TSA the names, titles, phone numbers, and email addresses of the new individual taking on that role.
provenance.transformation: Source retained verbatim; comparison inference separately labeled

provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.
